verdict.rationale: Isaac ships its own robotics foundation model, GR00T, with documented tooling to adapt and deploy it. That tooling covers collecting teleoperation demonstrations and converting them for GR00T post-training, refining GR00T via Isaac RL Post Training in Isaac Lab, checking platform compatibility with GR00T workflows, and packaging policies into portable deployment bundles for real hardware. However, the evidence never explicitly shows the model being wired into a runtime autonomy stack (e.g., a ROS 2 GR00T inference node), and the workflows are humanoid-focused. missing for 10: explicit documentation of running GR00T/VLA inference inside the robot's ROS 2 autonomy stack, support for third-party VLA models, non-humanoid embodiment guidance, independent hands-on corroboration of the integration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can integrate vision-language-action or robotics foundation models into my robot's autonomy stack through supported tooling

citations.quote: Refine pretrained robot foundation models such as Isaac GR00T with Isaac RL Post Training (RLPT).
Capture high-quality demonstrations through teleoperation in simulation or on a physical robot, then convert the data for GR00T post-training.
Package a policy’s compute graph and metadata into a portable deployment bundle to bring learned robot skills onto real hardware.
Determine if your humanoid platform meets the hardware and software requirements for integration with GR00T workflows and models.
They’re also adaptable through post-training for specific embodiments, tasks, and environments.
